title: Literary Reading II: Unreliable Narrator & Poetry
goal: Recognize when a first-person narrator's account of events can't be fully trusted, and read a short poem for figurative meaning, sound, and compression (saying a lot in very few words).

questions: List three specific phrases the narrator uses to insist they are "calm" or "reasonable." Why does a narrator who is genuinely calm rarely need to say so this many times?
Name one detail reported almost in passing — something another character says or does — that directly contradicts the narrator's version of themselves.
Reconstruct, in your own words, what probably actually happened that Thursday, reading around the narrator's own framing rather than trusting it.
